question: What post-subagent completion contract should OpenClaw support, if any, and how should it bound child output/history exposure, announcement mutation or suppression, and delivery-result visibility?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the payload, ordering, timeout behavior, redaction, plugin authority, and interaction with the rejected guard-hook PR are public API and security-boundary choices that automation should not lock in.

options.title: Generic Typed Delivery Boundary
options.body: Define one bounded hook or lifecycle contract for completion metadata and delivery decisions, avoiding the rejected PR's subagent-only guard-hook shape while preserving explicit security and audit semantics.

options.title: Generic Delivery Boundary First
options.body: Fold this into a broader product-driven output or delivery boundary so subagent completion filtering does not become a one-off public API.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Lifecycle Hooks
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer implementation until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43454 settles a unified lifecycle hook model across subagents, turns, and thresholds.

recommendation.title: Generic Typed Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Define one bounded hook or lifecycle contract for completion metadata and delivery decisions, avoiding the rejected PR's subagent-only guard-hook shape while preserving explicit security and audit semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent core subagent thread-binding work and the maintainer review closing the overlapping guard-hook PR make this the strongest available owner for the product/security boundary choice.
